question: A team is considering using Claude to triage inbound complaints, some of which allege safety issues. What should they do first?
options: A) Ask Claude to judge which complaints are serious enough to need a person, and follow that judgement.
B) Decide which complaint categories must always reach a person, and route those out of the automation.
C) Delay the project until every complaint category has been rewritten into a standard template form.
D) Automate the whole queue and review the outcomes at the end of the first quarter of operation.
correct_answers: B) Decide which complaint categories must always reach a person, and route those out of the automation.
explanations: Delegating the escalation boundary itself removes the safeguard the team is trying to build.
Correct. Defining the cases that require human handling has to happen before any triage is automated.
Standardising the intake forms does not address which complaints need a human at all.
A quarter of unreviewed safety complaints is exactly the harm this design needs to prevent.
